conventions.convention: Scalar distributions act complex-linearly on test densities; distributional densities act on scalar test functions. Pairings have no conjugation.
The operator relation uses (η,−ξ) in the nonzero conormal bundle. A defining function F gives η=DgFᵀτ and ξ=−DxFᵀτ.
Transforms have analytic submersive incidence projections, a nowhere vanishing analytic total density and weight, and properness of the data projection over each compact object support.
Pointwise Bolker requires a singleton full left fiber, including relation points outside the local chart, together with an injective left differential.
Gaussian packets use exp(iλ(x−y)·ω−λ|x−y|²/2), λ≥1 and |ω|=1. Regularity requires uniform exponential decay on neighborhoods of both the center and direction.

A normalized positive packet phase vanishes at its center, has object derivative −p there, and has a uniformly positive quadratic imaginary part. Ellipticity means a nonzero leading amplitude at the reference point.
The support-continuation hypothesis permits a C² hypersurface and absence of either oriented conormal; no reality assumption on the distribution is imposed.

load_bearing.statement: For a distribution localized sufficiently near the reference center, uniform exponential packet decay is independent of the normalized positive analytic phase and elliptic classical analytic amplitude. Bidirectional local superposition representations have polynomially bounded transition kernels and errors exponentially small in every fixed derivative.
At a relation point where dπL is injective, data Gaussian exponential regularity implies object Gaussian exponential regularity for distributions supported sufficiently near the paired object point.

If no relation point over the supplied nonzero data covector has object base in the compact support of u, that data covector is absent from WFA(Ru); the transpose packet is exponentially small in every fixed number of object derivatives near that support.
For every compactly supported distribution f, pointwise Bolker at (z₀,ζ₀;x₀,ξ₀) implies that absence of (z₀,ζ₀) from WFA(Rf) entails absence of (x₀,ξ₀) from WFA(f).
A distribution near 0 vanishing where xₙ<0 vanishes near 0 if either oriented normal is absent from its Gaussian analytic wavefront set. The assertion also holds with the half-spaces interchanged.

For compactly supported distributions or distributional densities, Gaussian exponential regularity is independent of the cutoff and equivalent under the analytic chart changes and pulled-back packet families used on this page, with the cotangent transformation of covectors.

Under the stated holomorphy, isolated critical-point and positive-imaginary-phase hypotheses, the localized integral has its complete stationary-phase expansion through order N−1, factorial coefficient and normalized remainder bounds, and exponentially small normalized remainder when N is proportional to λ.
For compact K in open U⊂Rⁿ, there are smooth compact cutoffs χN, N≥1, equal to one on a fixed neighborhood of K, with 0≤χN≤1 and |∂αχN|≤C(AN)^|α| for |α|≤N.

concerns.concern: The diagram draws θ upward and θ⊥ rightward. The cited and used convention is θ⊥=(−θ₂,θ₁), so for upward θ the perpendicular points left. The diagram reverses the oriented perpendicular convention used correctly in the algebraic proof.

The Statement calls Kλ the transpose localized data Gaussian but assigns ψ(X(v),v)=−q·p. For the Gaussian defined on this page, its transpose includes the factor exp(iλq·p), so the corresponding centered phase has value zero. Proof 2.2 explicitly strips this unit factor, and Proof 6.1 restores it; the Statement should identify Kλ as that phase-normalized transpose kernel.

The Statement uses c₀ both for the strictly positive quadratic lower-bound constant in 'r,c₀,d₀>0' and for the leading expansion coefficient in 'c₀=a(0)'. The amplitude value need not be positive or real. These are distinct constants and need distinct notation.

seams_checked.note: Read the supplier page and def-ip-2d-radon-transform. Both Radon examples use s=x·θ and θ⊥=(−θ₂,θ₁); their relation calculations preserve the signed-offset convention. They do not import Fourier-slice or normal-operator conclusions. The diagram orientation concern is recorded separately.

Read the supplier page and def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data. The missing-angle example retains openness and antipodal symmetry and proves only absence of a canonical pair for an invisible direction. It asserts no compact-support nullspace or stability conclusion.

Read the supplier page and def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform. The sphere example explicitly lies outside the simple-surface hypotheses and independently exhibits antipodal conjugacy and failure of global Bolker injectivity. No simple-surface injectivity theorem is applied to the sphere.
